Context

At a busy campus eatery, taking a payment is the core workflow. Unreliable connectivity shouldn’t mean losing a transaction or stopping the queue. OneTap Vendor is a desktop billing platform deployed across BITS Pilani eateries, built to handle that constraint.

Implementation

I worked on the desktop billing platform in Go and Fyne, using SQLite for local storage and sqlc for compile-time type-safe database access. The application supports UPI QR payments, bill splitting, and automatic backups.

TRANSACTION FLOW

Create bill→Persist locally→Sync when connected
The local billing flow continues through intermittent connectivity. Background synchronization uses retries and exponential backoff.

Offline synchronization

The important choice was making connectivity a synchronization concern rather than a requirement for recording a transaction. I engineered an offline-first synchronization engine with retry and exponential-backoff logic to prevent transaction loss during intermittent connections.

Type-safe SQL reduced the room for application and database contracts to drift, while automatic backups supported operational recovery.

Outcome

The platform serves 5,000+ students across campus eateries and supports $1.2M+ in annual payment volume.
